title: An Overview of Getting a Divorce in Colorado

content.rendered:
Divorce is never easy, but understanding the process can make it more manageable. If you’re considering filing for divorce in Colorado, this information will help you navigate each step, ensuring you’re well-informed and prepared for what lies ahead.

Understanding Divorce Laws in Colorado

To start, it’s essential to understand the basics of Colorado’s divorce laws. Colorado operates under a “no-fault” system, meaning that neither spouse has to prove wrongdoing to file for divorce. Instead, you must state that the marriage is “irretrievably broken.” This approach simplifies the process, allowing couples to focus on resolution rather than assigning blame.

Key Steps in a Colorado Divorce Process

Filing for Divorce

The first step in the divorce process in Colorado is to file a petition for dissolution of marriage with the appropriate district court. Either spouse can file a petition, and the petition should include basic information about both parties and any children from the marriage.

Serving Papers

Once the petition is filed, the next step is to serve divorce papers on the other spouse. This ensures that both parties are aware of the proceedings and have an opportunity to respond.

Response

The receiving spouse must respond to the divorce petition within 21 days of being served with the papers or signing a waiver of service. After mandatory financial disclosures are exchanged, the parties may choose to start negotiations for a settlement right away. If there are children from the marriage, parenting time and decision-making can be discussed.

Temporary Orders

The period of temporary orders starts when service occurs and ends when the divorce is final. A hearing on temporary orders may be necessary to establish temporary child custody, temporary spousal support, and temporary property use. These orders remain in effect until the court grants the divorce decree.

Discovery

Both parties exchange financial information and other relevant documents. This phase allows for transparency and fair division of assets.

Mediation

Mediation is required by Colorado courts in order to force divorcing spouses to at least attempt to resolve disputes amicably. A neutral third party helps both spouses come to an agreement on issues like property division, child custody, and support.

Trial (If Necessary)

If mediation fails, the case goes to trial. A judge will make the final decisions on contested issues.

Decree

Once all matters are resolved, either through mediation or trial, the judge issues a decree of dissolution, formalizing the end of the marriage.

Protecting Your Assets During a Colorado Divorce

Protecting your assets during a Colorado divorce is crucial. Begin by documenting all assets and debts. Work with a Colorado divorce attorney to understand what assets are considered marital property and which are separate. For example, a home purchased during the marriage is typically marital property, while an inheritance received by one spouse is generally considered separate. This distinction is vital in ensuring a fair division of property.

How Does Property Division Work?

Colorado is an “equitable distribution” state, which means that assets and debts acquired during the marriage are divided fairly, though not always equally. The court considers various factors, including each spouse’s economic situation, contributions to the marital estate, and the duration of the marriage. It’s essential to work with a knowledgeable Colorado divorce lawyer to ensure your interests are protected.

Implications of Divorce on Your Taxes in Colorado

Divorce can significantly impact your taxes. Changes in filing status, potential alimony payments, and the division of property are all factors to consider. It’s advisable to consult with a tax professional to understand how your divorce will affect your tax situation and to plan accordingly.

Child Custody: What Colorado Parents Need to Know

Child custody can be one of the most challenging aspects of a divorce. In Colorado, the primary consideration is the best interest of the child. The court looks at factors such as the child’s relationship with each parent, the parent’s ability to provide for the child’s needs, and the child’s adjustment to home, school, and community. Joint custody is common, but the specifics can vary based on individual circumstances.

Alimony Rules and Regulations in Colorado

Alimony, or spousal maintenance, may be awarded if one spouse needs financial support post-divorce. Factors influencing alimony in Colorado include the length of the marriage, the standard of living during the marriage, and the financial resources of both parties. Alimony can be temporary or permanent, depending on the situation.

Keeping Emotions in Check: The Psychological Aspects of Divorce

Divorce is not just a legal process but an emotional one as well. It’s common to experience a range of emotions, from anger to sadness. Seeking support from friends, family, or a therapist can be beneficial. Remember, taking care of your mental health is as important as handling the legal aspects.

How to Choose a Divorce Lawyer in Denver 

Choosing the right divorce lawyer in Denver, Colorado can make a significant difference in your experience and outcome:

Look for Experience

Choose a lawyer who focuses on family law and has extensive experience with Colorado divorce cases. The Drake Law Firm, for instance, has a team of seasoned professionals who understand the complexities of Colorado’s divorce laws.

Check Reviews and Testimonials

Client testimonials and online reviews can provide insights into a lawyer’s reputation and effectiveness. Look for consistent positive feedback and success stories.

Schedule Consultations

Meet with a few potential lawyers to discuss your case. Ask about their approach, fees, and how they handle communication. Feeling comfortable and confident in your lawyer is essential.

Assess Their Approach

Determine if the lawyer’s approach aligns with your goals. Some attorneys may emphasize mediation and settlement, while others are more aggressive in litigation.

Consider Costs

Understand the fee structure and ensure it fits within your budget. Some lawyers charge hourly rates, while others offer flat fees for specific services.

By following these steps, you can find a reliable divorce attorney in Denver to guide you through the process and protect your interests.

By understanding the Colorado divorce process and seeking the right support, you can move forward with confidence.
